files.description: Playwright tests for the people feature: list columns and per-person counts/actions, add via modal (name + searchable-select gender + intl date input), edit with pre-populated modal and round-trip of saved details, confirmed delete returning faces to the unassigned pool, and the per-person faces view with face removal. Adds a 'People — responsive' describe (P3) covering the contract width matrix for both /people and /people/<id>/faces, the labelled-card presentation of the six-column list, a long unbroken person name across both pages, the add-person dialog's containment and single scroll region, an in-progress dialog edit surviving a resize through the breakpoint, both person-faces peer-panel contracts and their ordering, and coarse-pointer selection in the person face gallery.

testContext: /people renders a .people-table (Name/Gender/Born/Faces/Photos/Actions); each row has a.person-name linking to /people/<id>/faces, two .stat-number cells (faces then photos), and [data-action=edit]/[data-action=delete] links carrying data-person-* attributes. Add/Edit use #addModal/#editModal (modal 'active' class) with #addPersonName/#editPersonName, a gender <select name=gender> hidden behind the searchable-select widget (click .searchable-select-display then .searchable-select-option; values: ''=Not specified, 1=Male, 0=Female), and an intl-date-input (visible #addPersonBirthdate/#editPersonBirthdate formats locale text into a hidden input[name=birthdate] on blur; en locale accepts MM/DD/YYYY). people_create ignores birthdate — only people_update persists it. Server flashes render as .flash-messages .alert-success ('Added X', "Renamed 'A' to 'B'", 'Deleted X', 'Person updated'). Delete and face-removal go through the global confirm dialog (#global-confirm-dialog + #confirm-dialog-confirm). The per-person faces view (/people/<id>/faces) renders .face-card[data-face-id] cards; clicking toggles .selected and a hidden checkbox; #remove-selected-faces confirms then submits #remove-form. Setup shortcuts: POST /api/people/create {name} → 201 {person_id}; POST /api/faces/assign {faces:[id], person:id, faceStatus:'ASSIGNED'} runs as a background task (taskq host required) — poll the person faces page for [data-face-id]. Unassigned-pool membership is read from /faces?threshold=1 by parsing each .suggestion-group's data-faces JSON (covers hidden clusters); face ids 1,11,13,18,26,37,41 are reserved by the face_assignment suite (they belong to Obama there) and must never be assigned from this suite. The 'No people yet' empty state needs zero people in the DB and concurrent suites create people, so it is not asserted. Unique Date.now()-suffixed names keep runs and parallel suites from colliding; afterAll deletes any leftovers via the UI. Responsive additions (2026-08-30): shared assertions come from generated_tests/_support/responsive.ts. /people registers no panel of its own; /people/<id>/faces registers #person-faces-actions and #person-faces-filters (toggles #person-faces-actions-toggle / #person-faces-filters-toggle), with #nav-menu-toggle last and carrying no data-nav-panel-toggle attribute. Below 640px responsive.css re-reads .people-table as labelled cards using each td's data-label through a ::before, and .people-table owns its own overflow-x. The person-faces filters are range inputs named min_similarity/max_similarity. A person's name reaches three places that must break it: the list cell, the page-header h1 and the empty-state sentence.
explanation: Generated manually from specs/people.yaml after inspecting templates/people/list.html, templates/people/faces.html, routes/people.py, static/people/list.js, static/people/faces.js, static/searchable-select.js, templates/components/intl_date_input.html + static/components/intl_date_input.js, routes/faces.py (FaceViewModel/data-faces payload), templates/base.html (flash markup), and the existing face_assignment suite (API helper conventions). Validated with npm run typecheck and a green run (5/5) against the isolated environment. 2026-08-30 (P3, responsive rollout): hand-written responsive scenarios added — not generated and not healed. One page bug was found and fixed with a scenario naming the cause: the person-faces empty state interpolates the person's name into a sentence, and an unbroken name there set the page's minimum width (672px at a 320px viewport). Full file green (15/15) via `npm run test:spec -- generated_tests/people/people.spec.ts --port 5302`.
